name: How do change orders usually affect custom home budgets?

mainEntity.name: Why do custom home change orders become so expensive, and how can I avoid them?
mainEntity.text: Why do custom home change orders become so expensive, and how can I avoid them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Change orders are one of the most common reasons custom home budgets drift upward. They become expensive because a single change can affect multiple trades, already-purchased materials, inspections, and the sequence of work. In a custom home, changing a window size, relocating a wall, or upgrading finishes can trigger revisions to structure, electrical, HVAC, plumbing, or exterior detailing. The best defense is to make as many decisions as possible before construction starts and to document any revisions carefully. Homeowners should also confirm that the contract explains how change orders are priced, approved, and scheduled. When the process is clear, the owner can control the tradeoff between flexibility and cost instead of discovering it after the fact.
acceptedAnswer.description: Change orders increase cost because they often affect labor already scheduled, materials already ordered, and related work downstream. In custom homes, even a small design change can trigger structural, electrical, plumbing, or finish revisions. The best way to reduce them is to finalize design choices early and keep the scope tight.
